name: sd-gpu
description: GPU-accelerated stable-diffusion.cpp build for image-tools, installed as a distinct `sd-gpu` command from a GPU release (Vulkan on Linux — runs on NVIDIA and AMD; CUDA 12 on Windows). The image-tools stable-diffusion.cpp provider prefers `sd-gpu` over the CPU `sd` when present, so its tier reports local-gpu and the capacity broker can arbitrate op-scoped GPU VRAM. Capability-gated: cleanly skipped on hosts with no GPU.
installHint: GPU build for the stable-diffusion.cpp backend: run `vrooli host install sd-gpu` on a GPU host. It installs a distinct `sd-gpu` launcher (into ~/.vrooli/opt/sd-gpu) alongside any CPU `sd`; the image-tools provider prefers `sd-gpu` when present, probes vulkan0/cuda0, reports tier local-gpu, and the capacity broker can then make op-scoped GPU VRAM claims. Linux uses the prebuilt Vulkan build (leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp publishes no Linux CUDA binary; CUDA on Linux is source-only). Uninstall sd-gpu to fall back to the CPU `sd` build.
notes: Pinned to leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp release master-709-92a3b73, matching the CPU `sd` tool. A distinct command (`sd-gpu`, not `sd`) so `vrooli host install sd-gpu` is not short-circuited by an existing CPU `sd` on PATH; the image-tools provider resolves `sd-gpu` ahead of `sd`. linux/amd64 = the x86_64-vulkan asset (NVIDIA + AMD via the Vulkan compute backend; verified live to detect an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, fp16-capable). windows/amd64 = the win-cuda12 asset. macOS has no matching target and is cleanly unsupported (same as the CPU `sd` tool). sha256 values are the GitHub release asset digests; the linux/amd64 archive was downloaded and verified.
